title: Missing Security-Fix Backporting for GitHub Actions Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2611.22519v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: GitHub natively supports workflow automation through GitHub Actions, now the dominant CI/CD tool on the platform. Yet keeping these workflows secure remains an ongoing burden: maintainers often patch a vulnerability on the default branch but leave the same flaw on the release and maintenance branches that downstream consumers continue to build from. Carrying a known fix onto these divergent branches, called backporting, is rarely done, and this paper presents the first large-scale empirical study quantifying the resulting gap. From a public corpus of GitHub Actions workflow histories, we mine 1,903,191 workflow-modifying commits, scan each before and after with the static scanner zizmor to identify 69,865 security fixes across 24,238 projects, and audit every release branch to check whether each fix was carried over. translated_title: GitHub Actions 工作流中安全修复回移植的缺失
translated_abstract: GitHub 通过 GitHub Actions 原生支持工作流自动化，GitHub Actions 目前是该平台上占主导地位的 CI/CD 工具。然而，保持这些工作流的安全性仍然是一项持续的负担：维护者通常只在默认分支上修补漏洞，而下游用户持续用于构建的发布分支和维护分支上却依然存在相同缺陷。将已知的修复迁移到这些分叉分支上，即所谓的“回移植”，却很少被执行。本文通过首次大规模实证研究量化了这一差距。我们从 GitHub Actions 工作流历史的公开语料库中挖掘了 1,903,191 个修改工作流的提交，使用静态扫描器 zizmor 对每个提交的前后状态进行扫描，在 24,238 个项目中识别出 69,865 个安全修复，并审计每个发布分支以检查修复是否被回移植。这一差距普遍存在：在审计的 474,490 个发布分支中，有 224,392 个仍然存在漏洞，而刻意的回移植行为非常罕见。
tldr: 本文首次大规模实证研究了 GitHub Actions 工作流安全修复在发布分支上回移植缺失的问题，发现近一半（224,392/474,490）已审计的发布分支仍存在已在默认分支修复的已知漏洞。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of missing security-fix backporting in GitHub Actions workflows, revealing that 224,392 of 474,490 audited release branches remain vulnerable despite known fixes on default branches.
